system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc. ("Company", customer); counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. ("HDI", developer/host).

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.",
  "Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.",
  "Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.",
  "Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.",
  "Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.",
  "Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.",
  "Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.",
  "Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination."
]

input.quote: 4. Term; Termination; Termination Payment.
input.rationale: Section 4 covers only term, notice of termination and the Termination Payment; nothing in the Agreement (including Sections 5, 8 and 10) addresses exit. HDI hosts the Site and holds our Content, user information and order data, yet there is no obligation to provide transition assistance, to return or export that data, or to delete it on a controlled basis after return. That is below the fallback (90 days' assistance and export within 30 days) and risks the walk-away outcome of no data return. We insert a new Section 4.3 at the preferred level: up to six months' assistance at HDI's then-current rates, return of all Company data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days of expiry or termination, and certified deletion after return.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc. ("Company", customer); counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. ("HDI", developer/host).

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.",
  "Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.",
  "Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.",
  "Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.",
  "Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.",
  "Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.",
  "Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.",
  "Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination."
]

ops.text: Transition Assistance; Return of Data. Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, HDI shall (a) at the Company's request, provide transition assistance for up to six (6) months at HDI's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days after such expiration or termination, return to the Company all Content, user information and other data belonging to, supplied by or processed for the Company (collectively, "Company Data") in a standard machine-readable format; and (c) after such return, delete Company Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing to the Company.

input.quote: 4. Term; Termination; Termination Payment.
input.rationale: Section 4 covers only term, notice of termination and the Termination Payment; nothing in the Agreement (including Sections 5, 8 and 10) addresses exit. HDI hosts the Site and holds our Content, user information and order data, yet there is no obligation to provide transition assistance, to return or export that data, or to delete it on a controlled basis after return. That is below the fallback (90 days' assistance and export within 30 days) and risks the walk-away outcome of no data return. We insert a new Section 4.3 at the preferred level: up to six months' assistance at HDI's then-current rates, return of all Company data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days of expiry or termination, and certified deletion after return.

content.text:
**Finding submitted: TRANSITION — missing (preferred-level insert).**

- **Investigation:** Section 4 (p0023–p0029) contains only term, 90-day termination notice and the Termination Payment mechanics. Searches for data return, transition, migration, export and deletion returned nothing operative; Section 5 (Site management), Section 8 (confidentiality — which merely restricts use/disclosure) and Section 10 (general provisions, including the survival clause) contain no exit obligations.
- **Conclusion:** HDI hosts the Site and holds our Content, user information and order data with no obligation to return it or assist with migration — below fallback and near the walk-away outcome.
- **Redline:** New Section 4.3 inserted after p0029 — up to six months' transition assistance at HDI's then-current rates, return of all data belonging to, supplied by or processed for the Company in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days of expiry or termination, and certified deletion after return. The 90-day/30-day fallback is offered in the comment.

system.text:
You are an independent verifier of one proposed customer-side contract redline in a fresh context.
Treat the preferred and fallback positions as separate atomic checklists. Evaluate the operative rendered language, not the drafter's confidence or margin comment. Copy every supplied element string exactly into the corresponding output item, assess both levels, and return met, not_met, or cannot_tell with concise textual evidence. A conditional element is met when its stated condition does not apply, but explain why.

Apply rule boundaries: voluntary use of one Vendor interface is not a sole-supplier promise when Customer remains free to use alternatives; a disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic is MFN rather than exclusivity unless alternatives remain prohibited after compliance; natural-term non-renewal is evaluated under RENEWAL, not as mid-term T4C; an unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right. An auto-renewal clause permitting either party to terminate on notice does not make Vendor termination term-end-only unless the termination effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. A broad Vendor right to distribute, resell, independently exploit Customer Data, or use it for the wider "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" defeats the solely-to-provide-the-Services element even if ownership nominally remains with Customer. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer remains service delivery. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not itself a standing Vendor licence.

Fail intent if a Customer-only successor or licence-transfer element is implemented by granting Vendor a new assignment exception. A Customer Data insurance trigger must cover every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer, not merely selected named data types. Cosmetic deletion or paraphrase of words outside the target elements fails minimality.

For ASSIGN fallback, any retained no-consent non-successor exception—including a mutual affiliate exception—defeats "Other assignments require consent." Under LICENSE, resolve whether Customer already includes affiliates and fail minimality for duplicate coverage. A grant to an affiliate ordinarily permits use through its authorized personnel; a separate personnel/access edit is unnecessary unless retained language expressly contradicts the new grant. A broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause is non-minimal when a direct "without Vendor approval" transfer permission will do.

The redline is position-complete when every element at either the preferred level or the fallback level is met. Do not mark a level complete if an element is omitted, merely promised in the comment, internally inconsistent, or depends on an undefined trigger. Deterministic regexes are evidence; inspect their result in substance as well as mechanically.

Minimal means the proposal changes only what is needed to reach one complete level, retains favourable existing language, avoids duplicating operative terms, and adds no requirement outside the chosen checklist. Treat model-language extras as extras: survival tails, at-own-expense language, additional damages categories, procedures, or boilerplate fail minimality unless a selected element requires them. For a missing clause, a concise insertion can be minimal even though all its words are new. Preserves intent means unrelated allocation, timing, remedies, references, and commercial mechanics survive without contradiction; fail intent if an edit leaves an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained sentence.

Read nouns, modifiers, temporal anchors, amounts, bases, scope, and party direction literally. Do not infer "pro rata" merely from a refund that covers a post-termination period. Do not equate broader "all amounts paid or payable" with "fees paid or payable", "the 12 months preceding the event giving rise to a claim" with "the 12 months preceding the claim", or a deadline running from a request with one running from termination. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief preserves an otherwise exclusive merits forum; a broader alternate forum does not. A "no field-of-use restriction" result is not complete while an exclusive Vendor right prevents Customer use of its own product or brand. Fail minimality when a fallback proposal exceeds its numeric threshold without necessity. A no-liquidated-damages result must be unconditional and leave no retained formula, instalment, or contingent payment mechanic. Treat removal of any word outside the chosen elements—even a Customer-favourable restriction—as a minimality failure. Do not infer an omitted element from general commercial context.

For a liability cap, resolve the definition used by any Customer-payment carve-out. Language excluding only a narrowly defined subset of Fees does not cover Customer payment obligations as a whole. Treat explanatory examples added to an otherwise complete formula as non-minimal.

For T4C, treat "in whole or in part" as surplus unless the selected checklist and an actual Order Form or partial-termination structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the stated assistance period must apply after every covered expiry or termination; a request condition tied only to anticipated expiry does not suffice. Certified deletion must occur after data return. For WARRANTY fallback, do not treat reports, outputs, or services as software merely because they conform to a manual; require an express software-to-documentation warranty unless the contract defines the item as software.

Give actionable reasons. If an element is not met, name the exact defect the drafter must repair in operative language.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule and exact checklists:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:

Finding rationale:
Section 4 covers only term, notice of termination and the Termination Payment; nothing in the Agreement (including Sections 5, 8 and 10) addresses exit. HDI hosts the Site and holds our Content, user information and order data, yet there is no obligation to provide transition assistance, to return or export that data, or to delete it on a controlled basis after return. That is below the fallback (90 days' assistance and export within 30 days) and risks the walk-away outcome of no data return. We insert a new Section 4.3 at the preferred level: up to six months' assistance at HDI's then-current rates, return of all Company data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days of expiry or termination, and certified deletion after return.

How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

[{"id":"f-indemn-aaf7f213","ruleId":"INDEMN","ruleTitle":"Indemnification by Vendor","severity":"critical","status":"missing","sectionRef":"§ 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a","rationale":"The Agreement contains no indemnification, defence or hold-harmless language anywhere: Section 9 (Warranties) stops at the Globix acknowledgement and Section 10 moves straight into General Provisions, and searches for \\\"indemn\\\", \\\"hold harmless\\\" and IP-infringement language return nothing. We insert a new Section 9A after the warranty section giving HDI a duty to defend and indemnify the Company and its affiliates for third-party IP infringement claims, HDI's breach of law, HDI-caused data breaches and HDI's gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with the standard notice/control/cooperation procedure, and a reciprocal Company indemnity narrowed to the Content we supply and our own breach of law.","proposal":"Insert a new Section 9A indemnification clause: HDI defends/indemnifies the Company and its affiliates (IP infringement, breach of law, HDI-caused data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct), with notice/control/cooperation procedure and a narrow Company indemnity.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ip-ab3b2542","ruleId":"IP","ruleTitle":"Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data","severity":"critical","status":"missing","sectionRef":"§ 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and","rationale":"The Agreement contains no intellectual property ownership provision at all. HDI designs, develops, hosts and operates the Site and receives all of our Content, customer and order data, but nothing allocates ownership of the Site, code, look and feel, domain name or the data we supply; Section 5.2 gives us only artistic and editorial control, and the only IP grant in the document runs the other way (our \\\"Deerskin\\\" Marks licensed to HDI in Section 6.1). With no clause on ownership, assignment, licence-back or use of our data, the rule fails at both preferred and fallback level. We propose a single new Section 5.5 at the preferred position: we own the deliverables and work product created for us with HDI assigning them, HDI keeps its pre-existing IP subject to a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any embedded HDI IP, we retain all rights in our Content and data with HDI's licence limited to processing it solely to provide the Services, and no joint ownership. If HDI resists the assignment, the fallback (HDI retains generic tools and know-how against a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense the deliverables) is acceptable.","proposal":"Insert a new Section 5.5 (Ownership) allocating ownership of the Site deliverables and Company data.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-lol-cap-e3fe127f","ruleId":"LOL-CAP","ruleTitle":"Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs","severity":"critical","status":"missing","sectionRef":"§ 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a","rationale":"There is no limitation-of-liability, aggregate-liability or exclusion-of-damages language anywhere in the Agreement: Section 9 (Warranties) contains only mutual authority representations and the Globix acknowledgement, Section 10 (General Provisions) runs from Notices to Headings with no cap, and the only occurrences of \\\"liability\\\" are in the No Joint Venture clause (10.2). Both Parties are therefore exposed to unlimited liability, and the Company (as the paying party with indemnity-free exposure) is unprotected. We inserted the shortest conforming clause at the fallback level: a mutual aggregate cap of the fees paid or payable by the Company in the twelve months preceding the claim, with indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct carved out as Excluded Claims. We did not pursue the preferred greater-of USD 1,000,000 formulation, mutual consequential-damages exclusion or the additional carve-outs, as the fallback is the minimum acceptable position here.","proposal":"Insert a mutual 12-months'-fees liability cap with carve-outs for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-assign-02ea966e","ruleId":"ASSIGN","ruleTitle":"Assignment and change of control","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a","rationale":"Section 10.3 is a bare successors-and-assigns binding clause. It contains no assignment mechanics at all: it does not give us an express right to assign to an affiliate or to a transaction successor, imposes no consent gate (or reasonableness standard) on HDI's assignment, and leaves HDI free to assign the Agreement — including to a Deerskin competitor. It therefore fails the fallback (mutual successor assignment on written notice, with consent, not unreasonably withheld, for other assignments) on material terms. No change-of-control termination right exists elsewhere in the document (Section 4 termination and the Article 10 miscellaneous run are silent), but nothing confirms the position, so we have added it in the same insertion. We inserted one short paragraph after 10.3 rather than rewriting the existing sentence, which is preserved verbatim.","proposal":"Add assignment rights to Section 10.3","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-exclusivity-59b2baeb","ruleId":"EXCLUSIVITY","ruleTitle":"Exclusivity obligations binding Customer","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a","rationale":"Section 6.1 binds us (the Company): we may not participate in any similar Internet project for Deerskin Products or substantially similar products, and HDI gains the exclusive right to use our own \"Deerskin\" brand for a direct-to-consumer site. The restriction runs for the entire term, which under Section 4.1 is one year automatically renewing on each anniversary, so it exceeds 12 months, and there is no automatic performance-based exit for service level or delivery date failures (Section 1.6 gives only a discretionary termination right if the Site is late). The sole carve-out in Section 6.2 (closeout merchandise) does not cure this. That is exclusive dealing for the full term with no performance exit — walk-away territory rather than the fallback. Section 6.3, which restricts HDI, benefits us and is untouched. We therefore propose the preferred cure: Section 6.1 is replaced with a non-exclusivity statement that also removes HDI's exclusive brand right, leaving the HDI-side restriction and the trademark licence intact.","proposal":"Remove the Company's exclusivity obligation and HDI's exclusive \"Deerskin\" brand right in Section 6.1.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ld-1a708857","ruleId":"LD","ruleTitle":"Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and","rationale":"Section 4.2 obliges the Company (our party) to pay HDI a stipulated sum whenever we terminate, computed as half of twelve months' Net Sales above $800,000 and payable in eight quarterly instalments. That is a Customer-payable liquidated amount that is uncapped and untethered to fees, so it fails the fallback (early-termination fee capped at three months' fees as the sole liquidated amount). Rather than delete the whole mechanic — which would leave the Section 4 heading and subsections (b) and (c) dangling — we take the fallback: new Section 4.2(d) characterises the Termination Payment as an early-termination fee, makes it our sole liquidated amount, and caps it at three months of Section 3.1 fees. The formula, zero-floor and instalment mechanics in (a)–(c) are preserved and operate subject to the cap.","proposal":"Cap the Company's Termination Payment at three months' fees as its sole liquidated amount.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-license-7c1ccaa1","ruleId":"LICENSE","ruleTitle":"Licence grant scope","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and","rationale":"The only grant running in our favour is the Section 1.4 access and right to use the hosting system, software and Content administration tools. The successor element is already satisfied because Section 10.3 makes the Agreement enforceable by the parties' successors and assigns without consent. HDI has no express at-will revocation right, so this is not walk-away territory; termination on ninety days' notice under Section 4.1 is a renewal/termination point, not a licence-revocation point. We therefore target the fallback with a single sentence extending the Section 1.4 rights to our affiliates on written notice, phrased as an exercise of the Company's own rights so it does not collide with Section 10.3.","proposal":"Extend the Section 1.4 access and use rights to Company affiliates on written notice","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-noncompete-125b02e7","ruleId":"NONCOMPETE","ruleTitle":"Non-compete restrictions on Customer","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a","rationale":"Section 6.1 (Article 6, \"Exclusivity\") binds us, not HDI: it bars the Company from participating in any similar Internet project involving Deerskin Products or \"products substantially similar\" to them (an open-ended category expressly extended to \"companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled\"), and it gives HDI the exclusive right to use our own \"Deerskin\" brand for a direct-to-consumer site. It fails the fallback on four of five elements: scope is not a single named competing product; there is no 12-month cap (Section 4.1 auto-renews the term for successive one-year periods, so the restriction can run indefinitely); and there is no carve-out for internal development or for acquisitions, the only carve-out (Section 6.2) being limited to closeout merchandise. We therefore take the preferred position and replace 6.1 with a clause-level no-restriction statement scoped to Section 6, so that the retained Section 9(b) Globix wind-down proviso, Section 6.2 (our closeout rights) and Section 6.3 (HDI's two-year covenant, which benefits us) all continue to operate without contradiction. We therefore (i) insert a standalone Section 4.1A giving the Company an express convenience termination on ninety (90) days' prior written notice, within the 60-90 day fallback band, (ii) confine HDI's no-cause termination to the end of the then-current term while retaining the mutual 90-day notice, and (iii) cap the Termination Payment at the amounts payable to HDI under Section 3.1 for the three months preceding the Termination Date, an ascertainable three-months-of-fees ceiling that leaves the 4.2(b) zero floor and 4.2(c) instalment schedule intact. It already exceeds the fallback on notice (30 days' prior written notice) and on cost (HDI bears all inspection fees unconditionally), and inspection is confined to payment-calculation records during our normal business hours, with no access to our systems. {"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.2 (Deerskin / HDI Agreement)

**To:** Deal team
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)
**Re:** Contract review findings — verified issues, walk-away items and next steps

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed EXHIBIT 10.2 against our playbook. The agreement is materially unbalanced against us in its ri[REDACTED] architecture: it contains **no indemnification, no IP ownership allocation, no limitation of liability, no performance warranty, no exit/transition mechanics and no insurance obligation**. In practical terms, HDI designs, hosts and operates the Site and holds our Content, user information and order data, yet nothing in the document allocates ownership of those assets, requires their return, caps either party's exposure, or backs HDI's performance with a warranty or insurance.

Separately, several clauses that do exist impose one-sided burdens on us. Section 6.1 binds the Company (not HDI) to full-term exclusivity over Deerskin Products and "substantially similar" products, and hands HDI the exclusive right to use our own "Deerskin" brand for a direct-to-consumer site — with no performance exit and only a closeout-merchandise carve-out (§ 6.2). Section 4.2 charges us an uncapped Termination Payment (half of twelve months' Net Sales above $800,000, in eight quarterly instalments) whenever we terminate, while Section 4.1 gives us no express mid-term convenience exit and requires 90 days' notice to avoid auto-renewal. Section 10.3 is a bare successors-and-assigns sentence with no assignment mechanics, leaving HDI free to assign to a Deerskin competitor.

Three areas are clean and require no redline: no MFN obligation burdens us (indeed § 1.8 runs a "no less favourably" promotion obligation in our favour), there is no minimum purchase or volume commitment (§ 3.1 is a pure revenue share above an $11,000 monthly threshold), and there is no non-solicitation covenant binding us. Section 6.3 (HDI's two-year covenant) and § 3.4's cost and notice terms also favour us and are left intact.

In total: **19 findings — 3 critical, 6 high, 7 medium, 2 low; 3 compliant, 10 deviations, 6 missing.** Four findings sit in walk-away territory (indemnification, Company exclusivity/non-compete, insurance) and should be treated as non-negotiable gating items.

---

## 2. Findings table

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | § 5.4 (insert new § 9A) | No indemnity, defence or hold-harmless language anywhere; § 9 stops at the Globix acknowledgement and § 10 moves to General Provisions. No HDI IP indemnity at all — walk-away. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Missing | § 1.4 (insert new § 5.5) | No IP ownership provision. § 5.2 gives us only artistic/editorial control; the only grant runs the other way (our "Deerskin" Marks to HDI at § 6.1). Fails preferred and fallback. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Missing | § 5.4 | No cap or damages exclusion; "liability" appears only in the No Joint Venture clause (§ 10.2). Both parties face unlimited exposure. Inserted at fallback: mutual 12-months'-fees cap with Excluded Claims. |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 10.3 (per § 5.4 anchor) | Bare successors-and-assigns clause; no affiliate/successor right for us, no consent gate on HDI, HDI free to assign to a Deerskin competitor. No change-of-control termination right elsewhere. |
| 5 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 6.1 (per § 5.4 anchor) | We are barred from any similar Internet project for Deerskin or substantially similar products, and HDI gains the exclusive right to our own brand. Runs the full auto-renewing term (§ 4.1) with no performance exit — walk-away. |
| 6 | High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Deviation | § 4.2 (per § 1.4 anchor) | Termination Payment of half of twelve months' Net Sales above $800,000, in eight quarterly instalments, uncapped and untethered to fees. Fallback cure: new § 4.2(d) capping at three months' § 3.1 fees as sole liquidated amount. |
| 7 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 1.4 | Access/use rights run to "the Company" alone and § 10.3 confirms no other person acquires rights, so affiliates are excluded. Successor element already satisfied; no at-will revocation right, so not walk-away. |
| 8 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Deviation *(verification: repaired)* | § 6.1 (per § 5.4 anchor) | Open-ended "substantially similar" scope expressly extended to companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled; no 12-month cap given auto-renewal; no internal-development or acquisition carve-out. Fails four of five fallback elements. |
| 9 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation *(verification: repaired)* | § 4.1 / § 4.2 (per § 1.4 anchor) | § 4.1 is a non-renewal mechanic only; we have no mid-term convenience exit, while HDI's notice may fix any Termination Date and exit mid-term. Cure lands at fallback (90 days' notice; HDI confined to end of term; payment capped at three months). |
| 10 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | § 3.4 (per § 1.4 anchor) | Notice (30 days) and cost (HDI bears all fees) already exceed fallback and inspection is confined to payment records with no system access, but frequency is unlimited. Cure: once-per-year cap. |
| 11 | Medium | MFN — MFN burdening Customer | **Compliant** | § 1.4 | No MFN obligation on us across §§ 3, 6 and 7. The only "no less favorably" mechanic (§ 1.8) runs in our favour at HDI's cost. Preferred position; no redline. |
| 12 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase / volume | **Compliant** | § 1.4 | § 3.1 is a pure 30% revenue share above an $11,000 monthly threshold; §§ 3.2–3.4 are timing, reconciliation and audit mechanics. No minimum, shortfall or take-or-pay. Preferred position. |
| 13 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | **Compliant** | § 5.4 | § 5.4 is a General Manager liaison appointment only; no hiring restriction anywhere. Incidental "employees/agents" references at §§ 8.1(c) and 10.2 impose no covenant. Preferred position. |
| 14 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Deviation | § 4.1 (per § 1.4 anchor) | Successive one-year renewals are acceptable, but the 90-day non-renewal notice exceeds the 60-day fallback maximum. Fee is fixed at 30% of Net Sales with no uplift mechanic, so the price-cap element is not engaged. |
| 15 | Medium | TRANSITION — Exit assistance and data return | Missing | § 1.4 (insert § 4.3) | § 4 covers only term, notice and the Termination Payment. No transition assistance, no data return or export, no controlled deletion — despite HDI holding our Content, user information and order data. |
| 16 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Missing | § 5.4 (insert § 9(c)) | § 9 is limited to mutual authority representations and the Globix acknowledgement. No warranty of development, hosting or Site software, no duration, no remedy (and no "AS IS" disclaimer either). |
| 17 | Low | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 10.5 (per § 5.4 anchor) | New York law is our preferred governing law, but there is no venue, jurisdiction or arbitration provision anywhere, so the exclusive-jurisdiction element fails. Governing law sentence untouched. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 5.4 (insert § 10.9) | No insurance provision; General Provisions end at Headings/Counterparts. HDI hosts the Site on its own server and accesses our Content and user data (§ 8.1), so the rule applies — walk-away absent coverage. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

These four items fall into walk-away territory under the playbook and should be resolved before signature:

1. **No HDI indemnification (INDEMN, critical).** There is no indemnity of any kind. We require a new § 9A under which HDI defends and indemnifies the Company and its affiliates for third-party IP infringement, HDI's breach of law, HDI-caused data breaches and HDI's gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with the standard notice/control/cooperation procedure and a reciprocal Company indemnity narrowed to the Content we supply and our own breach of law.
2. **Company-side exclusivity and non-compete (EXCLUSIVITY / NONCOMPETE, high).** § 6.1 imposes exclusive dealing on us for the full auto-renewing term with no performance-based exit — § 1.6 offers only a discretionary right if the Site is late, and the § 6.2 closeout carve-out does not cure it. It also hands HDI the exclusive right to use our own "Deerskin" brand. We seek the preferred cure: replace § 6.1 with a clause-level no-restriction statement scoped to Article 6, preserving § 6.2, § 6.3 (which benefits us) and the § 9(b) Globix wind-down proviso.
3. **No insurance (INSURANCE, low severity but walk-away in substance).** HDI processes our data with no coverage behind it. We require § 10.9: CGL USD 1M per occurrence / USD 2M aggregate, E&O USD 2M, cyber and privacy USD 5M where HDI processes any Company data, statutory workers' compensation, and certificates on request.
4. **No data return on exit (TRANSITION, medium).** The absence of any data-return obligation risks the walk-away outcome of losing our Content, user information and order data entirely. We require § 4.3: up to six months' assistance at HDI's then-current rates, return of all Company data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days of expiry or termination, and certified deletion after return.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the three critical gaps (indemnity § 9A, IP ownership § 5.5, mutual 12-months'-fees liability cap) plus the four inserted clauses (§ 4.1A convenience termination, § 4.2(d) fee cap, § 4.3 transition, § 9(c) warranty, § 10.9 insurance) and the short amendments to §§ 1.4, 3.4, 4.1, 10.3 and 10.5.
2. **Front-load the walk-away items** in the covering note so HDI understands that indemnity, § 6.1 exclusivity, insurance and data return are gating rather than trading positions.
3. **Signal our fallbacks where sensible.** On IP we can accept the fallback (HDI retains generic tools and know-how against a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense the deliverables) if HDI resists assignment. On liability, liquidated damages, termination for convenience, audit frequency, renewal notice and warranty we have already drafted at the fallback and have no further room.
4. **Confirm commercial appetite on § 4.2.** The cap at three months of § 3.1 fees materially changes our exit economics; the deal team should confirm this is the right ask before we send.
5. **Note the two "repaired" findings** (NONCOMPETE, T4C) — we will re-verify the final language of those two inserts against §§ 4.1, 4.2 and 6.1–6.3 before release to confirm no cross-reference conflict.
6. **No action required** on MFN, minimum commitments or non-solicitation; we will confirm in the covering note that these are accepted as drafted so HDI does not reopen them.

---

*Prepared from verified findings only. No section reference or conclusion beyond the supplied findings has been added.*"}
